newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cuts home-buying savings rate. [CORRECTED 18:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: France cuts home-buying savings rate. [CORRECTED 18:10 GMT]

text.p: France on Monday cut the interest rate on home-buying savings plans to 4.25 percent from 5.25 percent, effective January 23 (corrects from February 23), to bring the administrative rate in line with market conditions, the Finance Ministry said.
The move, which was expected, will also allow home loans at 4.80 percent which could give a boost to the flagging housing market.
Existing home-buying savings plans, Plans d'Epargne-Logement (PEL) will be unaffected.
"The French economy currently enjoys historically low interest rates. In this framework it seemed legitimate to review the rate on home-buying savings plans," the statement said.
It added that with home loans at 4.80 percent "borrowers can benefit from housing loans at the lowest rate ever since this product was created".
